extra_vocab.zh: 預期的、未來可能成為…的
extra_vocab.en: likely to become something in the future
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 prospective employees 指「可能會被錄用的人」，也就是明天來面試的應徵者，不是現在已在公司上班的員工。prospective 放在名詞前面，表示這個人或事物「將來有可能成為」該身分。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: prospective 只放在名詞前面修飾（a prospective client），不能說 The client is prospective。

collocations.zh: 準員工、可能被錄用的人

example.en: We pay travel costs for prospective employees who live far away.
example.zh: 我們替住得遠的準員工支付交通費。

example.en: Her job is to follow up with every prospective client weekly.
example.zh: 她的工作是每週追蹤每一位潛在客戶。

example.en: The agent showed the prospective buyer around the building yesterday.
example.zh: 仲介昨天帶可能的買家參觀了這棟大樓。

examples.en: Please send the schedule to all prospective employees by Friday.
examples.zh: 請在星期五前把時程表寄給所有可能被錄用的人。

examples.en: Our sales team is meeting prospective customers in Osaka next week.
examples.zh: 我們的業務團隊下週要在大阪拜訪潛在顧客。

examples.en: The prospective merger will be announced after the board meeting.
examples.zh: 預定中的合併案將在董事會後公布。

confusable.diff: perspective 是名詞「觀點、看法」，prospective 是形容詞「預期的、潛在的」，拼法很像但意思完全不同。
confusable.usage: perspective 是名詞（from a different perspective）；prospective 是形容詞，放在名詞前。

example.en: Her perspective on the problem helped the team find a solution.
example.zh: 她對這個問題的看法幫助團隊找到了解決辦法。

similar.diff: potential 也是「潛在的」，更常用在客戶、風險、問題；prospective 較強調「預期將成為」某個身分。

example.en: We identified several potential customers during the trade show.
example.zh: 我們在展覽中找到了幾位潛在客戶。

similar.diff: future 只是「未來的」，不一定表示可能性；prospective 帶有「很可能會成為」的意思。

example.en: Please send this notice to all future tenants of the building.
example.zh: 請把這份通知寄給大樓所有未來的房客。

example.en: Poor weather is a potential risk for the outdoor event.
example.zh: 天氣不好是戶外活動的潛在風險。

example.en: Each applicant must complete the online form before the interview.
example.zh: 每位應徵者面試前都必須填完線上表格。

example.en: The final candidate will meet the team on Monday.
example.zh: 最後一位候選人星期一會和團隊見面。

derived.link: prospective 的詞幹，prospect 是「前景」；加 -ive 變形容詞，像 act → active

extra_vocab.en: a situation where too many people or vehicles fill a place and move slowly
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 heavy congestion 指市區道路施工造成的嚴重塞車，所以應徵者可能遲到。這是描述交通狀況的常用說法。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: congestion 是不可數名詞，不加 s，也不加 a；要說「一次塞車」可用可數的 a traffic jam。

example.en: Traffic congestion costs local businesses millions of dollars each year.
example.zh: 交通壅塞每年讓當地企業損失數百萬美元。

example.en: A new subway line should ease congestion on the main roads.
example.zh: 新的地鐵線應該能紓解主要道路的壅塞。

example.en: Drivers entering the city center must pay a congestion charge.
example.zh: 開車進入市中心的駕駛必須繳交擁擠費。

examples.en: Heavy congestion on the highway delayed the delivery trucks this morning.
examples.zh: 高速公路上的嚴重壅塞讓貨車今早延誤。

examples.en: The city plans to reduce congestion in the downtown area.
examples.zh: 市府打算減少市中心的壅塞。

examples.en: Port congestion has slowed down shipments from Asia to Europe.
examples.zh: 港口壅塞拖慢了從亞洲到歐洲的貨運。

confusable.diff: suggestion 是「建議」，結尾和 congestion 很像（-gestion），但意思無關。

example.en: The manager welcomed every suggestion about improving the morning commute.
example.zh: 經理歡迎任何改善早晨通勤的建議。

similar.diff: traffic jam 是口語、可數的「塞車」；congestion 較正式，是不可數的整體狀況。

example.en: A traffic jam on the bridge delayed the client's arrival.
example.zh: 橋上的塞車讓客戶晚到。

similar.diff: gridlock 指車流完全動彈不得，比 congestion 更嚴重。

example.en: Gridlock around the stadium lasted for nearly two hours after the game.
example.zh: 比賽結束後，體育場周邊的車陣癱瘓了近兩個小時。

example.en: Traffic is lighter after eight o'clock in the evening.
example.zh: 晚上八點後車流比較少。

example.en: We apologize for the delay in processing your order.
example.zh: 我們為處理您的訂單延誤致歉。

example.en: A large crowd gathered outside the convention center.
example.zh: 一大群人聚集在會議中心外面。

derived.link: congestion 去掉 -ion 就是動詞，像 suggestion → suggest

senses.en: a state in which a place is too full and things move slowly
senses.distinguish: 旁邊常出現 traffic、road、port 等字。

example.en: Airport congestion caused long delays for several international flights.
example.zh: 機場壅塞造成幾班國際航班嚴重延誤。

senses.en: a blocked nose or chest when you are ill
senses.distinguish: 出現在感冒、藥品、請病假的情境。

example.en: Cold medicine can relieve congestion and help you sleep better.
example.zh: 感冒藥可以緩解鼻塞，幫助你睡得更好。

extra_vocab.en: opposite to what was said or expected
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 Contrary to my earlier email 表示「和我先前信上說的相反」，是更正自己先前說法的客氣用語，後面緊接新的正確資訊。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: contrary to 後面接名詞、代名詞或 what 子句（contrary to what I said），介系詞是 to，不是 with。

example.en: The final cost was far higher, contrary to our estimate.
example.zh: 與我們的估計相反，最後的成本高出許多。

example.en: The delay did not hurt us; on the contrary, it helped.
example.zh: 這次延誤沒有傷到我們，正好相反，還有幫助。

example.en: Unless you hear anything to the contrary, the meeting starts at nine.
example.zh: 除非你聽到相反的消息，否則會議九點開始。

examples.en: Contrary to last year's rule, staff may now work from home.
examples.zh: 與去年的規定相反，員工現在可以在家工作。

examples.en: The two reports reached contrary conclusions about the new product.
examples.zh: 兩份報告對這項新產品得出相反的結論。

confusable.diff: contrast 是「對比」（in contrast to），強調兩者的差別；contrary to 是「與…相反、矛盾」。
confusable.usage: in contrast to 用來比較兩件事的不同；contrary to 用來說明和某個說法、預期完全相反。

example.en: In contrast to last year, this year's budget is much smaller.
example.zh: 和去年相比，今年的預算小很多。

similar.diff: unlike 只是「和…不同」，不一定相反；contrary to 強調和說法或預期相反。

example.en: Unlike our competitors, we offer free shipping on every order.
example.zh: 和競爭對手不同，我們每筆訂單都免運費。

example.en: The two teams took opposite sides in the discussion.
example.zh: 兩個團隊在討論中持相反的立場。

example.en: We received conflicting reports about the delivery date.
example.zh: 我們收到對交貨日期互相矛盾的報告。

example.en: Please read the instructions on the reverse side.
example.zh: 請閱讀背面的說明。

example.en: Contrary to rumors, the company has no plan to close the plant.
example.zh: 與傳言相反，公司沒有關閉工廠的計畫。

example.en: The client gave us contrary instructions in two separate emails.
example.zh: 客戶在兩封不同的信裡給了我們相反的指示。

example.en: I expected delays, but the contrary happened: everything arrived early.
example.zh: 我原本預期會延誤，結果正好相反，全都提早到了。

extra_vocab.en: an official paper that shows you finished a course of study
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 diplomas 指應徵者的畢業證書。因為學歷已由人資查核過，所以面試時不必攜帶正本。

example.en: The office keeps copies of all diplomas in a locked cabinet.
example.zh: 辦公室把所有畢業證書的影本放在上鎖的櫃子裡。

example.en: The position requires a high school diploma and two years of experience.
example.zh: 這個職位要求高中畢業證書和兩年經驗。

example.en: It took him three years to earn a diploma in nursing.
example.zh: 他花了三年才取得護理文憑。

example.en: The college offers a one-year diploma program in business.
example.zh: 這所學院開設一年期的商業文憑課程。

examples.en: Applicants must show their original diploma on the first day of work.
examples.zh: 應徵者上班第一天必須出示畢業證書正本。

examples.en: She is studying for a diploma in graphic design at night.
examples.zh: 她晚上在進修平面設計的文憑。

examples.en: Please upload a copy of your diploma to the online form.
examples.zh: 請把畢業證書的影本上傳到線上表格。

confusable.diff: diplomat 是「外交官」，字形和 diploma 很像，但指的是人。

example.en: The diplomat attended a trade meeting with several business leaders.
example.zh: 這位外交官出席了和幾位企業領袖的貿易會議。

similar.diff: degree 是大學以上的「學位」；diploma 是畢業證書，也可以是程度較低的文憑。

example.en: A bachelor's degree is required for the senior engineer position.
example.zh: 資深工程師的職位需要學士學位。

similar.diff: certificate 是修完某項課程或通過考試的「證書」，通常比 diploma 短期。

example.en: The training center gives each participant a certificate at the end.
example.zh: 訓練中心在最後會發給每位參加者一張證書。

example.en: Her main qualification is five years of experience in logistics.
example.zh: 她主要的資歷是五年的物流經驗。

example.en: Most graduates from this program find jobs within three months.
example.zh: 這個課程的多數畢業生三個月內就找到工作。

example.en: Please submit your official transcript with the application form.
example.zh: 請連同申請表一起繳交正式成績單。

senses.en: an official paper that shows you finished school or a course
senses.distinguish: 指實體的證明文件，常和 show、bring、copy 等動詞一起出現。

example.en: He hung his diploma on the wall of his new office.
example.zh: 他把畢業證書掛在新辦公室的牆上。

senses.en: a qualification you get from a course that is shorter than a degree
senses.distinguish: 常寫成 a diploma in + 領域，指課程或資格本身。

example.en: The diploma in logistics takes about one year to complete.
example.zh: 物流文憑課程大約一年可以修完。

extra_vocab.en: working carefully and with a lot of effort
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 a diligent worker 是前主管推薦信裡對應徵者的稱讚，表示她做事認真、有責任感。diligent 是推薦信和績效評語的常用字。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: diligent 後面可接 in 或 about + V-ing，例如 be diligent in checking the data。

example.en: We are looking for a diligent worker for the night shift.
example.zh: 我們在找一位勤奮的員工來上夜班。

example.en: After diligent effort, the team solved the shipping problem.
example.zh: 經過勤奮的努力，團隊解決了出貨問題。

example.en: Diligent research helped us find the best supplier.
example.zh: 認真的調查幫助我們找到最好的供應商。

examples.en: Her supervisor described her as a diligent and reliable employee.
examples.zh: 她的主管形容她是認真又可靠的員工。

examples.en: He is diligent about answering every customer email within a day.
examples.zh: 他很認真，每封顧客來信都在一天內回覆。

examples.en: A diligent assistant checked every figure before the meeting started.
examples.zh: 一位認真的助理在會議開始前核對了每一個數字。

confusable.diff: intelligent 是「聰明的」，diligent 是「勤勉的」，兩字結尾相似，但一個說能力、一個說態度。

example.en: He is intelligent, but he often forgets to finish his tasks.
example.zh: 他很聰明，但常常忘記完成工作。

similar.diff: hardworking 是最通用、口語的「努力工作的」；diligent 更正式，也帶有細心的意思。

example.en: The hardworking staff stayed late to finish the quarterly report.
example.zh: 認真工作的員工留到很晚完成季報告。

similar.diff: conscientious 強調「有責任感、一絲不苟」，語氣比 diligent 更偏重細心與責任。

example.en: A conscientious clerk always double-checks the numbers before sending invoices.
example.zh: 認真負責的職員在寄出發票前總會再核對數字。

example.en: She is a reliable colleague who always meets deadlines.
example.zh: 她是個可靠的同事，總是準時交件。

example.en: Our dedicated team works around the clock during the sale.
example.zh: 促銷期間，我們盡心投入的團隊日夜工作。

example.en: An efficient process saves both time and money.
example.zh: 有效率的流程能同時節省時間和金錢。

derived.link: diligent 去掉 -t 加 -ce，變成名詞，像 patient → patience
diligent + -ly，形容詞變副詞，像 careful → carefully

extra_vocab.zh: 吸引、有吸引力（appeal 的過去式）
extra_vocab.en: to be interesting or attractive to someone
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 appealed to me especially 表示這位應徵者特別吸引我、讓我印象深刻。appeal to + 人 是「對某人有吸引力」，主詞是事物或人，不是主動去吸引的動作。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 「吸引」的 appeal 一定要接 to + 人（appeal to me），不能直接接受詞（✗ appeal me）；要直接接受詞可用 attract。

example.en: This design appeals to younger customers around the world.
example.zh: 這個設計吸引了世界各地較年輕的顧客。

example.en: The court rejected two appeals from the former employees.
example.zh: 法院駁回了前員工的兩項上訴。

example.en: We are appealing the decision to the review committee.
example.zh: 我們正向審查委員會對這項決定提出申訴。

example.en: The company offered an appealing salary and flexible hours.
example.zh: 公司提供有吸引力的薪資和彈性的工作時間。

example.en: Low prices appeal to customers who shop online every week.
example.zh: 低價吸引每週上網購物的顧客。

example.en: The product has broad appeal across all age groups.
example.zh: 這項產品對各年齡層都有廣泛的吸引力。

example.en: Employees may file an appeal within ten days of the decision.
example.zh: 員工可以在決定後十天內提出申訴。

examples.en: The idea of a four-day week appealed to most of the staff.
examples.zh: 一週工作四天的構想吸引了大部分員工。

examples.en: Bright packaging appeals to children, but parents choose the product.
examples.zh: 亮眼的包裝吸引小孩，但選擇產品的是家長。

examples.en: Her experience in logistics appealed to the hiring manager immediately.
examples.zh: 她的物流經驗立刻吸引了招聘經理。

confusable.diff: appear 是「出現、似乎」，拼法和發音都和 appeal 很像，但意思不同。
confusable.usage: appear 是不及物動詞，不需要接 to 表示吸引；appeal 要接 to + 人 才是「吸引」。

example.en: A new error message appeared on the screen this morning.
example.zh: 今天早上螢幕上出現了新的錯誤訊息。

confusable.diff: apply 是「申請、應用」，如 apply for a job；appeal 是「吸引、上訴」。

example.en: Please apply for the position before the end of the month.
example.zh: 請在月底前申請這個職位。

similar.diff: attract 直接接受詞（attract customers）；appeal 要加 to（appeal to customers）。

example.en: The festival attracts thousands of visitors from other countries.
example.zh: 這個節慶吸引了數千名來自其他國家的訪客。

example.en: A strong brand can attract talented employees.
example.zh: 強大的品牌能吸引有才華的員工。

example.en: The new proposal did not interest the board.
example.zh: 新的提案沒有引起董事會的興趣。

example.en: The company made an attractive offer to the engineer.
example.zh: 公司向這位工程師開出了有吸引力的條件。

example.en: This job offer does not appeal to me at all.
example.zh: 這份工作邀約完全吸引不了我。

example.en: The appeal of the new phone is its long battery life.
example.zh: 這款新手機的吸引力在於電池續航力久。

senses.en: to be attractive or interesting to someone
senses.distinguish: 後面接 to + 人，主詞是事物或人，常見於行銷與招聘。

example.en: The flexible schedule appealed to many experienced applicants.
example.zh: 彈性的時程吸引了許多有經驗的應徵者。

senses.en: to ask people strongly to do something
senses.distinguish: 後面常接 to + 人 + to V，出現在公告與新聞。

example.en: The manager appealed to staff to save energy during the summer.
example.zh: 經理呼籲員工在夏季節約能源。

senses.en: to ask a higher authority to change a decision
senses.distinguish: 常接 against 或直接接 a decision，出現在法律、人事申訴。

example.en: The supplier appealed against the fine but lost the case.
example.zh: 供應商對罰款提出上訴，但敗訴了。

extra_vocab.zh: 專攻、專門從事（specialize 的第三人稱單數）
extra_vocab.en: to work mainly in one particular area or field
extra_vocab.note: 在這篇裡 someone who specializes in logistics software 指受邀的應徵者都是專攻物流軟體的人，符合 Alan 的要求。who 後面的動詞要配合 someone，所以用 specializes。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: specialize 後面接 in（不是 on 或 at）+ 名詞或 V-ing；主詞是第三人稱單數時要加 s。

example.en: She specialized in tax law before she joined our firm.
example.zh: 她在加入我們事務所之前專攻稅法。

example.en: Specialized training is required for anyone who operates this machine.
example.zh: 任何操作這台機器的人都需要專業訓練。

example.en: We are specializing in cold storage for food products now.
example.zh: 我們現在專門從事食品的冷藏儲存。

example.en: Many small shops specialize in handmade leather goods.
example.zh: 許多小店專門販售手工皮製品。

example.en: We specialize in repairing industrial printers and copy machines.
example.zh: 我們專門維修工業用印表機和影印機。

example.en: Technicians receive specialized training before using the new equipment.
example.zh: 技術人員在使用新設備前會接受專業訓練。

examples.en: Our consulting firm specializes in helping small businesses grow online.
examples.zh: 我們的顧問公司專門協助小型企業在網路上成長。

examples.en: I specialize in customer service for the financial industry.
examples.zh: 我專攻金融業的客戶服務。

examples.en: We need an engineer who specializes in network security.
examples.zh: 我們需要一位專攻網路安全的工程師。

confusable.diff: specify 是「明確指定、說明」，拼法相近，但不是「專攻」。

example.en: Please specify the delivery date in your reply email.
example.zh: 請在回信中明確指出交貨日期。

similar.diff: focus on 是「把重心放在」，可以是暫時的；specialize in 表示長期專長。

example.en: The company will focus on logistics software next year.
example.zh: 公司明年將專注於物流軟體。

similar.diff: concentrate on 強調「集中精神或資源」，不一定是專業領域。

example.en: We plan to concentrate on markets in Southeast Asia.
example.zh: 我們打算集中在東南亞市場。

example.en: An expert in customs law will join the meeting.
example.zh: 一位海關法規專家將參加會議。

example.en: The staff gave us professional advice on shipping.
example.zh: 員工就運送問題給了我們專業的建議。

example.en: We hired an experienced manager to lead the project.
example.zh: 我們聘請了一位有經驗的經理來帶領專案。

derived.link: specialize 的詞幹，special 是「特別的」；加 -ize 變動詞，像 modern → modernize
special + -ist，做專門領域的人，像 artist、scientist
special + -ty，變成名詞，指「特別擅長的事」
specialize 去掉 -e 加 -ation，變名詞，像 organize → organization
